The 8 RAW notes above describe what `tubuild create` produced. That output was NOT used: at 36 members the generated preamble is unusable, so the merged source was hand-assembled from the 36 shards plus src/d_a_gmch.c in ROM-ascending order. Read the file's own header comment for what was and was not reconciled.

MEASURED, and it is the one thing in this TU that is not a shard's own spelling: `#include "common.h"` sits BEFORE daGmch_c.h. common.h and math/Matrix.h both define Matrix4x3 under the single MATRIX4X3_DEFINED guard and whichever is seen first stands. daGmch_c.h reaches math/Matrix.h through Model.h, so without that line ordinal 34 (_ZN8daGmch_c13InitResourcesEv) sees the structured Matrix3x3+Vector3 spelling, splits `mMatrix = IDENTITY_MATRIX4X3` into a 9-word ldm/stm plus a CSE tail and comes out 0x1f0 against the cartridge's 0x1d4 -- 35/36. The shards reached the flat s32[12] spelling through decl_common.h -> common.h; this include replaces that route and restores 36/36.

decl_common.h is deliberately NOT included. It declares 7 of this TU's 26 auto-named members and 3 of those 7 contradict the byte-matched definitions: func_ov081_02126950 as (void*, void*) against (int*, void*), func_ov081_02127708 as int(char*) against void(C*), and func_ov081_0212777c as (void*, int) against (char*, int). Including it would be three `illegal function overloading` errors pointed at the definitions rather than at the header, which is the ov002/Player and ov006/dScMgLuigi_c precedent.

compiler_only_output.reason: mwccarm emits the base-object destructor beside the licensed D1/D0 pair when the destructor is out of line under `#pragma defer_codegen off`. The cartridge has no daGmch_c D2 at all -- a grep of the whole config/ tree for MoneybagD2, daGmch_cD2 and 8daGmch_cD2 returns no rows, no third destructor address appears in _ZTV8daGmch_c, and all_symbol_homes() returns nothing for it -- so it is homeless and a plain deadstrip is the right disposition.

types.h gives Vector3 a declared destructor, so any TU that odr-uses one re-emits its vague-linkage D1. Ordinal 5 (func_ov081_02126700) holds a Vector3 local and ordinal 34 another. The cartridge keeps one copy at arm9:0x020072c0 and an enrolled source already owns it; rombuild compares this object's body against those cartridge bytes and refuses anything but byte-identical vague-linkage output before discarding the duplicate.
